h1: RTJ Rentals: a corporate housing website that feels like home
title: RTJ Rentals: Corporate Housing Website | Rakib Hasan
summary: A WordPress site that helps companies, insurers and families find furnished, pet-friendly temporary housing across Georgia and South Carolina.
alt: RTJ Rentals homepage on a laptop.

p_client.t: RTJ Rentals provides corporate housing and short-term apartments for companies, families and people facing temporary displacement, such as after a house fire or flood. Its homes are fully furnished, pet-friendly and in prime locations across Georgia and South Carolina. Co-founders Rodlyn and Tanya built the business around personal service and smooth insurance housing, so guests feel at home from the first night.

p_challenge.t: RTJ serves three very different audiences: HR teams placing staff, insurance adjusters arranging emergency housing, and families in a stressful situation. Each needs different information, fast. Before, enquiries came in by phone and email with the same questions every time, and the old one-page site couldn't show individual homes. The site had to look premium enough for corporate clients while staying warm and reassuring for displaced families.

p_built.t: I designed the site around the homes themselves. Each property has its own page with photos, amenities, location and pet policy, so visitors can compare options without calling first. Clear paths lead corporate clients, insurers and families to the information they need, and enquiry and availability forms built with Gravity Forms send requests straight to the team.

The design uses large photography and calm, simple layouts to reflect the company's focus on comfort and care. Every page was built responsive for phones, where many displaced guests first search. The site runs on WordPress with Elementor Pro and Crocoblock, so the team can add properties and update details themselves. Wordfence and regular backups keep it secure, and every page launched with unique titles, descriptions and SEO basics.

p_result.t: The team now adds and updates properties themselves, and most enquiries arrive through the forms with dates, pets and budget already filled in, so fewer calls go on basic questions.

p_testi.t: > "Rakib understood that our guests are often in a hard moment. The site feels calm and personal, and our team can finally update it without help." — Tanya, RTJ Rentals

p_client.t: Villa Lapierrot is a recently renovated holiday home in Provence, between the Dentelles de Montmirail and Mont Ventoux. p_built.t: The design leads with the landscape: large photography of the pool, terrace and surrounding vineyards, with short text that lets the images do the selling. I organised the content around what guests care about most: the bedrooms, the pool, outdoor living, and how close the villa is to local attractions in Provence.

Every page is responsive, since many holiday searches start on a phone, and the site was optimised for searches about villas in the area. The owners can update photos, prices and seasonal details themselves in Elementor.

p_result.t: Returning guests now book direct through the villa’s own site, and the gallery does the selling before anyone sends a message.

p_testi.t: > "Our guests tell us the website made them fall in love with the villa before they arrived. Exactly what we wanted." — Villa Lapierrot owners

p_challenge.t: Sabiha needed a warm, credible site that explained her mentoring programme clearly and made booking a first discovery call feel easy.

p_built.t: A soft, editorial design with a homepage that leads with her mentoring promise, a "What we offer" section, an About page with her story, and a discovery call form on every page.

p_result.t: Sabiha now has a professional home for her mentoring programme, and discovery calls are booked straight from the site.

p_testi.t: > "Rakib made the whole process easy and the site looks exactly like my brand." — Sabiha Ozbay

h1: Tatiana Megard: a minimalist portfolio for an avant-garde designer
title: Tatiana Megard: Fashion Designer Portfolio | Rakib Hasan
summary: An elegant, minimalist WordPress portfolio that lets a fashion designer's collections speak for themselves.
alt: Tatiana Megard website on a laptop

p_client.t: Tatiana Megard is a fashion designer whose work treats fashion as a craft. Her collections focus on physical materiality and sharp, abstract geometric lines, reworking classic clothing with an avant-garde approach.

p_challenge.t: A designer's portfolio must feel like her work, and anything decorative gets in the way. The site had to be quiet, precise and image-led, while still explaining her creative process.

p_built.t: A sleek portfolio layout with high-quality images of each collection, generous white space and simple navigation between collections, process and contact. It's responsive on every device and optimised for search to raise her visibility in the fashion industry.

p_result.t: Tatiana now sends clients and stockists to one elegant portfolio instead of scattered social posts.

p_testi.t: > "Elegant and simple, exactly as I imagined. Rakib listened to every detail." — Tatiana Megard

h1: (in)extenso: a portfolio website for a publishing-led design studio
title: (in)extenso: Graphic Design Studio Website | Rakib Hasan
summary: A French-language WordPress site for a graphic design studio, presenting its project portfolio and services for cultural and publishing clients.
alt: (in)extenso website on a laptop

p_client.t: (in)extenso is a graphic design studio led by Lisa Boxus, who has over 25 years of experience. It specialises in publishing, with deep knowledge of printing and finishing, and creates communication materials, visual identities, illustrations, books and objects. Clients include the Théâtre Royal du Parc, Pierre de Lune and the Jean Dubuffet Foundation.

p_challenge.t: Designers judge other designers' websites harshly. The site had to showcase a strong body of print work on screen and explain how the studio supports clients from first idea to finished object.

p_built.t: A portfolio-led site with a projects section, a services page, an about page, an FAQ and a contact page. A "Tested and approved" testimonials section adds social proof, and links to Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn connect the site to the studio's wider presence.

p_result.t: The studio now presents its projects in a format clients remember, and new enquiries reference specific work they saw.

p_testi.t: > "A thoughtful designer who understands creative work. Great result." — (in)extenso

name: Tündérkehely

h1: Tündérkehely: a calm website for yoga, sound and healing
title: Tündérkehely: Yoga & Sound Therapy Website | Rakib Hasan
summary: A Hungarian-language WordPress site for a wellness practice, bringing classes, sound journeys, events and booking into one calm place.
alt: Tündérkehely website on a laptop

p_client.t: Tündérkehely offers yoga, sound therapy and grief counselling, in person in Budapest and Gyál and online. It runs group yoga classes, individual, paired and group sound journeys, and events such as floating sound baths, sound bowl relaxation sessions and women's yoga retreats.

p_challenge.t: A wellness site has to feel restful while doing practical work: listing classes in two locations, keeping an events calendar current, and sending people to book.

p_built.t: A calm, simple site with sections for services, events, pricing and booking, a blog and contact. Booking connects to the practice's external booking platform, and a newsletter sign-up keeps visitors coming back for new events.

p_result.t: Classes and events are now easy to find in both locations, and bookings come straight from the calendar.

p_testi.t: > "Professional, fast, communicative. I love my website. I recommend the work with him." — Abonyi Tünde Anná, Tündérkehely
